current morphologic criteria used for the identification of uterine leiomyomas in HLRCC patients are largely irreproducable and lack sufficient robustnes to serve as a reliable trigger for 2SC biomarker testing or further family/personal medical history inquiry.
the morphologic criteria for uterine LMS in HLRCC are not robust enough to trigger genetic testing.

current morphologic criteria for identifying hereditary leiomyomatous renal cell carcinoma (LRCC) syndrome-associated leiomyomas are not robust and do not perform well in identifying patients with this condition.

the development of a clinically relevant, reproducible and robust diagnostic schema for the identification of HLRCC-associated uterine leiomyomas.
the identification of uterine leiomyomas in the context of HLRCC syndrome, which has a high rate of malignancy.
the identification of uterine leiomyomas in the setting of the hereditary leiomyomatous and renal cell carcinoma syndrome.

the current morphologic criteria used for identifying uterine LMSs in HLRCC are not robust enough to serve as the sole trigger for genetic testing or family/personal history inquiries, although they can be considered in combination with other features.

the morphologic criteria proposed for the diagnosis of HLRCC-associated uterine LMS are not clinically robust and should not be used to guide patient care.

the morphologic criteria used by the HLRCC consortium to define syndromic uteri LMs is not robust enough to be used as a trigger for genetic testing.
